name: Big Black
label: Touch and Go
lede: A Northwestern student, a Roland drum machine and two guys poached from Naked Raygun made six years of the ugliest, most exact noise in America, then quit on purpose the moment everybody wanted them.

eras.title: One kid, one living room, one drum machine
eras.text: Big Black started as Steve Albini's solo project while he was a student at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois. He played everything himself, let a drum machine keep time, and sent the results out in packages meant to offend.

years.h: Steve Albini records Lungs alone over spring break
years.p: Steve Albini, a Northwestern student, spends spring break 1981 recording six songs in his living room, playing guitar and bass over a drum machine. Touch and Go's own bio stresses it wasn't his first band.

years.h: Lungs EP · Ruthless Records, 1,500 copies
years.p: Steve Albini's solo recordings come out on Chicago's Ruthless Records. According to Wikipedia, copies came stuffed with inserts: dollar bills, used condoms, Bruce Lee photos and bloodied paper.

eras.title: Stealing from Naked Raygun
eras.text: Albini turned the project into a band by borrowing two members of Chicago's Naked Raygun. The rules were set early: no contracts, no advances, no manager, no booking agent, no lawyer. Big Black booked its own tours and paid its own bills.

years.h: Jeff Pezzati and Santiago Durango join Steve Albini
years.p: [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]] singer Jeff Pezzati takes bass and guitarist [[Santiago Durango|00aa2c29-22a9-4e55-a01b-e51896a379a3]] comes over from the same band. [[Pat Byrne|6321b6f8-e574-480b-82d7-e5bf1a838fc5]], later of [[Urge Overkill|120e728a-4078-47b7-a31c-d581ade28bde]], plays real drums on the next record.

years.h: Bulldozer EP, in a galvanized sheet-metal sleeve
years.p: The first 200 copies of Big Black's Bulldozer come in galvanized sheet metal, a nod to [[Public Image Ltd|68950696-ee9a-49b2-a8c2-d1d6c19355cc]]'s Metal Box. Steve Albini later said he sorta conned Fever Records into paying for it.
years.xp: Iain Burgess engineered Bulldozer. The song Cables is about a slaughterhouse in Montana, where Albini grew up, and Pigeon Kill about an Indiana town poisoning its pigeons. Most of Big Black's songs worked like that: short stories about the worst of America, many lifted from real events.

years.h: Big Black books its own first US tour
years.p: No agent, no manager: Big Black takes itself across the country in 1984, setting up the run of records it would license to Homestead.

years.h: Jeff Pezzati leaves Big Black for his job and Naked Raygun
years.p: Jeff Pezzati quits at the end of 1984. His day job and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]], the band he fronted, both needed him more.

eras.title: The Roland hits on one and three
eras.text: With Dave Riley on bass the line-up locked in, and the drum machine became the band's signature: programmed to hit on the beats rock drummers leave alone. Big Black got louder, sharper and more notorious, and fell out with the label selling its records. Chicago snubbed them at first, so they skipped Chicago, and Albini's badmouthing of the Metro got them banned there for good.

years.h: Racer-X EP · Homestead Records
years.p: Big Black's deal with Homestead has no contract and no advance, and the band keeps the rights to its recordings. Racer-X is the first record under it.

years.h: Dave Riley joins on bass, bringing funk from Detroit
years.p: [[Dave Riley|c29ae450-90ca-4593-8892-1fd5e47e507a]] had worked at a Detroit studio where [[George Clinton|84683370-5eae-418b-acd8-883ac028a8a0]] and [[Sly Stone|a833e001-7c3b-491f-b7d4-2ef367837b95]] recorded. His bass gives Big Black its low end and a groove nobody expected.

years.h: Rema-Rema single comes free with Forced Exposure No. 9
years.p: Big Black covers the [[Rema-Rema|c34623b5-8d04-4b5b-87dc-2be531975d10]] song Rema-Rema on a 500-copy single packaged with issue No. 9 of the zine Forced Exposure, where Steve Albini also wrote.
years.xp: Albini's writing was its own provocation. His column in the Chicago zine Matter, Tired of Ugly Fat?, tore into the local scene and split readers down the middle.

years.big: 500 copies meant for radio, sold as collector's items
years.h: Homestead sells Big Black's free Il Duce promos
years.p: Homestead pressed 500 12-inch copies of the Il Duce single to give to radio. They turned up in shops at collector prices. Steve Albini posed as a buyer to prove it, and Big Black cut ties with Homestead.
years.xp:
The break also ended Big Black's relationship with Homestead's parent distributor, Dutch East India Trading. For a band whose entire business model was a handshake, selling the promos was the one unforgivable move.

Big Black would release its last records on Touch and Go, run by Albini's close friend [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]].

years.src: Wikipedia · Michael Azerrad, Our Band Could Be Your Life
years.h: The drum machine credited as a member: Roland
years.p: Big Black's Roland TR-606 is programmed to accent beats one and three instead of rock's two and four. Club soundmen feared it would blow their speakers, and the band had to talk them into it.
years.xp: Shows opened with firecrackers and Steve Albini counting in with a profanity. Albini notched his metal picks with sheet-metal clips so each stroke hit twice, and the band's hands bled from slamming steel strings. Durango described the job as assembling noises made by guitars, not playing them.

years.h: Atomizer, Big Black's first album · Homestead
years.p: Big Black's first full-length, with Kerosene, Jordan, Minnesota and Bazooka Joe. It sold 3,000 copies soon after release, more than the band expected.
years.xp:
Jordan, Minnesota is about the 1983 child sex abuse scandal in that town. Live, Steve Albini acted out the victim's part while the band stretched the noise out. The records also drew accusations of racism and homophobia over slurs in the lyrics; Albini defended them as satire, and critics didn't all buy it.

[[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] later listed Atomizer among his favorite records.

years.h: Big Black's first European tour wins over the UK press
years.p: Blast First handles Big Black in Europe, and the 1986 tour gets the band raves in the British music papers, well ahead of its reputation at home.

years.h: The Hammer Party collects Lungs and Bulldozer
years.p: Homestead puts Big Black's first two EPs, Lungs and Bulldozer, on one record, The Hammer Party.

eras.title: Quit while they're loudest
eras.text: Big Black planned its own ending a year out: Santiago Durango was going to law school, so the band scheduled a final year of records and tours. Major labels came calling; Riley said the money would have meant it wasn't Big Black anymore.

q: I was tired of working shitty jobs.
years.h: Santiago Durango's law school sets Big Black's end date
years.p: Santiago Durango is headed to law school in fall 1987, and the band decides to stop rather than replace him. They spend the year finishing everything.

years.h: Headache EP, Big Black's first on Touch and Go
years.p: Headache comes in a black plastic body bag with forensic photos of an accident victim on the cover, and a sticker warning buyers it isn't as good as Atomizer.

years.h: Big Black covers Wire, Cheap Trick and Kraftwerk
years.p: Touch and Go releases the Heartbeat single, a [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]] cover, and He's a Whore / The Model, covering [[Cheap Trick|9f870653-72b0-4c6d-8c59-439a95963e09]] and [[Kraftwerk|5700dcd4-c139-4f31-aa3e-6382b9af9032]] with guitars playing the synth parts.

years.h: Pukkelpop on Steve Albini's 25th birthday
years.p: Big Black plays Belgium's Pukkelpop festival on Steve Albini's 25th birthday, on a bill with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]].

yt: Steve Albini on drugs and drinking in Big Black
years.h: Dave Riley smashes the drum machine at CBGB
years.p: Dave Riley's drinking was ruining shows, according to Wikipedia's account of the breakup, and at a CBGB gig he smashed the Roland drum machine.

years.h: Wire's Bruce Gilbert and Graham Lewis join Big Black in London
years.p: At a sold-out 1,300-capacity London show, [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]]'s Bruce Gilbert and Graham Lewis come out for the encore of Heartbeat, Wire's own song. Tapes from the London dates became Pigpile.

years.h: The Last Blast: Big Black's final show in a Seattle steam plant
years.p: Big Black ends in an abandoned Seattle power plant, smashing its instruments and setting off firecrackers. In the crowd: [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]], [[Mark Arm|3f99d2df-8859-4249-8a70-84fe04c5a096]], [[Kim Thayil|dd676aae-658e-42f3-b3d9-8660ea29198d]] and Sub Pop's Bruce Pavitt.
years.xp:
Larry Reid produced the show. Roland Barker and James Husted played synths from the plant's catwalks, and poet Jesse Bernstein read before Big Black came on. Bruce Pavitt wrote that he cut his hand grabbing a piece of broken guitar.

Steve Albini mixed the concert film, The Last Blast.

q: We wanted to make filthy music.
years.h: Songs About Fucking comes out after Big Black is gone
years.p: Side one, Happy Otter, recorded in London; side two, Sad Otter, in Chicago on gear that became Electrical Audio. The first pressing of 8,000 made it Big Black's best seller.
years.xp:
Albini said rock and roll originally meant dirty songs about exactly that, and when people pushed back on the title, the band said no, that's the name of the record. Durango called it the biggest insult to the music industry he knew of. The cover image came from Japanese manga a friend imported; Australia's Au Go Go label covered it with a sticker reading Please remove.

Robert Christgau marveled that the band could crush the competition and quit at the same time.

years.h: The Rich Man's Eight Track Tape puts Atomizer on CD
years.p: Touch and Go's CD gathers Atomizer, Headache and the Heartbeat single for the format Big Black never made a record for.

eras.title: The engineer, the lawyer and the stroke
eras.text: The members scattered in very different directions. Albini became the most famous recording engineer in independent music, Durango a lawyer, and Riley's life was upended by a stroke. Big Black's catalog stayed with Touch and Go.

years.h: Steve Albini forms Rapeman and records Surfer Rosa
years.p: Steve Albini starts [[Rapeman|899dea17-b403-42e0-9673-2623c40081af]] with [[David Wm. Sims|c6c8a98f-9cfb-4fad-a657-880245ff15d3]] and [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]] of [[Scratch Acid|75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0]], and engineers the [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]]' Surfer Rosa. Later come [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]] and his Chicago studio, Electrical Audio.
years.xp: Albini refused producer credits and royalties, calling them an insult to the band, and charged indie bands low day rates. Over the next decade he recorded [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]], [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]], [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]], [[PJ Harvey|e795e03d-b5d5-4a5f-834d-162cfb308a2c]] and [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s In Utero.

years.h: Santiago Durango makes Arsenal records in law school
years.p: Santiago Durango releases two EPs as Arsenal on Touch and Go while at law school and plays with [[Boss Hog|57648c1f-335d-4216-ba82-508b23b3bcf4]]. As a lawyer his clients included Touch and Go and Cynthia Plaster Caster; later he became an appellate defender in Ottawa, Illinois.

years.h: Pigpile, live from Big Black's last London dates
years.p: Touch and Go releases Pigpile, recorded on Big Black's final 1987 tour, alongside a single covering the Mary Jane Girls' In My House.

years.h: Kurt Cobain brings a chunk of Steve Albini's smashed guitar
years.p: At the In Utero sessions, Kurt Cobain shows Steve Albini a piece of the guitar Albini smashed at Big Black's last show in Seattle in 1987. Albini told NME that Cobain had been the kid who asked for it.

years.h: Dave Riley's stroke, first misreported as a suicide attempt
years.p: Dave Riley has a stroke in 1995 that at first is wrongly reported as a suicide attempt. He loses the ability to walk and later writes a blog called Worthless Goddamn Cripple.
years.xp: Riley kept making music, with Algebra Suicide, Bull, Flour and in 2004 his own project, Miasma of Funk. In 2006 he published a book, Blurry and Disconnected: Tales of Sink-or-Swim Nihilism.

years.h: Big Black's four-song reunion for Touch and Go's 25th
years.p: Steve Albini, Santiago Durango and original bassist Jeff Pezzati play Cables, Dead Billy, Pigeon Kill and Racer-X at Touch and Go's 25th anniversary festival in Chicago. Albini said it would not happen again.
years.xp: Albini explained that skipping it would have been an insult to Touch and Go, damning the label with faint praise. [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]]'s touring left no time for real rehearsal, so the set stayed short.

eras.title: Two deaths
eras.text: Big Black's bassist and its founder died within five years of each other. Albini died with a new Shellac album days from release.

years.h: Dave Riley dies at 59
years.p: Dave Riley, Big Black's bassist from 1985 to 1987, dies on Christmas Eve 2019 at 59, of squamous cell carcinoma in his throat and lungs, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at 61
years.p: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at 61, ten days before [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]]'s To All Trains comes out on Touch and Go.
